So my test garden (just to see if the land could handle it) is more successful than I ever would have expected. Every time I go out there, I come back with a bucket full of produce.

I have frozen enough ears of corn to fill a 5 gallon bucket (honestly, I lost count how many) and have something like 10 more in the queue waiting to be frozen or eaten. Some of my corn stalks are making their fourth ears right now (did not know they would do that) but I don't expect them to be very large or useful in any way. I've left one row to the fall for popcorn and seed (I hope, maybe). My littlest corn stalk is maybe two feet tall and it's finally produced like 5 ears but they're too tiny to do anything with and at ground level. All the same, I'm cheering it on because "you go, little guy."

A deer managed to get in and chew most of the corn tassels away. And some of the sunflower leaves. One sunflower doesnt' have enough leaves to do anything because it's just a stalk now but it's still green so I'm leaving it. Two others were broken but are still kicking and have blooms. The others are like 12 feet tall and constantly covered with bees. Some of these bees just kick it overnight on the flowers and dont' even go home. I've counted upwards of 12 blooms popping up on one of the plants, haven't bothered to count the others. The top blooms are full on open and facing east, though.

I have more eggplants than I know what to do with and that's just two plants.

I've finally managed to get tomatoes now that I've covered them with netting. Birds and critters kept eating them. Not a lot of tomatoes. Yet.

The cauliflower plants are finally starting to show me the cauliflower. Too small and young to harvest but they're starting.

I've had to cut up about a quart and a half of peppers to freeze. That'll be fine since I use them in recipes instead of salads.

Cucumbers. MY. GOD. I'm drowning in cucumbers. My three cucumber plants are putting out 5 to 10 cucumbers per week. Each week, I'm getting at least one cucumber that is no less than 1.5 feet long (and not bitter, either). I've made 2.5 gallons of bread and butter pickers and 1.5 gallons of regular pickles. I still have cucumbers left over.

The onions gave up a long time ago. I fully expected them to but it was just a test to see and learn so no loss.

Any the roses... I get an occasional bloom (nothing like when they first all popped up) every few days but the hips that are waiting for first frost... some of them are as big around as a nickle. And there's a lot of them.

I also rescued a dragonfly from the tomato nets. Got to hold him for about a minute before he flew off.

Herbs and strawberries had to be moved because the tree stump I planted them next to needed to be ground away. The rosemary died but the sage and oregano are thriving. Mint got moved to the screened porch and is doing much better. The basil is going crazy. The strawberry plants survived the move but are not producing (at least this year). I fully expected the dill to die but it's actually still around. Not very big but still alive.
